name: Forlorn Ridge
summary: Alliance and Horde positions line the slopes of Forlorn Ridge in southwestern Azshara. The ridge rises above the coast.

sections.title: A Contested Vantage
sections.body:
Forlorn Ridge rises above western Azshara, shaped like an ancient volcano long quiet. From its heights, you can see the coast and the ruined elven estates below.

The ridge commands this stretch of land, so Alliance and Horde forces have built encampments and outposts along its rugged slopes. They watch each other across the bluffs.

faq.answer: Forlorn Ridge rises above the wilderness and coastal roads of southwestern Azshara.

faq.q: Why are the Alliance and Horde fighting over this ridge?
faq.answer: Forlorn Ridge commands wide views across western Azshara. From its heights, either faction can watch troop movements between the coastal ruins and inland passes. So both have fortified positions on its slopes.

faq.q: Was Forlorn Ridge originally a volcano?
faq.answer: Forlorn Ridge's rugged shape suggests it may once have been a volcano. It has long been quiet and overgrown.

angles.text: As an Alliance soldier, you can watch Horde movements spilling eastward from the Barrens and Ashenvale. Forlorn Ridge gives you early warning and a view of the field.
As a member of the Horde, you can use footholds along Forlorn Ridge to help secure Azshara's rugged borderlands just north of Durotar against Alliance incursions.
